mainTopic: Wine left in a gentile's care: deposits, seals, double seals, and sealed barrels of כותים
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about non-Jewish wine. Ordinary gentile wine (סתם יינם) is forbidden for any benefit. Wine a Jew left with a gentile is forbidden to drink but permitted for benefit. The גמרא tests that middle ruling from both sides. It first sets the case where the gentile set aside a special corner. Then it brings בר קפרא's ברייתא, taught to רבי יוחנן by רבי תנחום of פרוד, which permits even drinking. רבי זירא explains that the two sources reflect a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבנן about wine locked or sealed in a gentile's courtyard, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן then argue whether one seal, or a double seal, protects wine, and רבא shows what counts as a seal within a seal. Finally, a ברייתא tells how the חכמים came to permit sealed barrels of כותים wine. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge that ruling, with the contradicting source coming on the next amud.

steps.title: Ordinary gentile wine is forbidden for benefit and carries impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that סתם יינם is אסור בהנאה and makes things טמא with טומאת משקין when there is a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ordinary wine of gentiles is forbidden for any benefit, and a quarter-log of it makes things impure the way liquids do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting a ברייתא that lists the laws of different kinds of non-Jewish wine. Here it gives the rule for ordinary wine of gentiles, meaning wine we don't know was poured for idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though we don't know this wine was used for עבודה זרה, the חכמים forbid all benefit from it, not just drinking. Its טומאה is the lighter kind, טומאת משקין, and it only applies when there is a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary wine of gentiles, not known to have been used for idol worship
Forbidden for any benefit, not only for eating or drinking
A quarter of a לוג, a standard liquid measure

phrases.english: Their ordinary wine (of gentiles)
is forbidden for benefit,
and it makes things impure with the impurity of liquids, when there is a quarter-log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section, which was listing laws of gentile wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סתם יינם is forbidden for benefit, and a רביעית of it carries טומאת משקין.

steps.title: Wine a Jew left with a gentile is forbidden to drink but allowed for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if a Jew deposits his wine with a gentile, drinking it is forbidden but benefit is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone leaves his wine with a gentile, he may not drink it, but he may benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a middle ruling for a Jew's wine that was left in a gentile's care. It is not fully forbidden, and it is not fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the wine was out of the Jew's sight, there is some worry about it, so drinking is forbidden. But it started as Jewish wine, so it is not treated as harshly as סתם יינם, and benefit stays permitted. The rest of this section will test this middle ruling from both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits, leaving something in someone else's care
Permitted for benefit, for example selling it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels here: סתם יינם is forbidden for benefit. Wine deposited with a gentile is forbidden to drink but permitted for benefit. Next, the גמרא will challenge this middle ruling.

phrases.english: One who deposits his wine with a gentile:
it is forbidden to drink,
but it is permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְקִיד יֵינוֹ אֵצֶל גּוֹי אָסוּר בִּשְׁתִיָּה וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ruling in the same ברייתא, covering a less severe case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine a Jew deposited with a gentile is forbidden to drink but permitted for benefit.

steps.title: A משנה treats deposited produce as the gentile's own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the permission to benefit from a משנה that says produce left with a gentile counts as the gentile's produce for שביעית and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: if someone deposits his produce with a gentile, it is treated like the gentile's own produce for the laws of שביעית and מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling of step 2 using a משנה about produce left with a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes the gentile may have swapped the Jew's produce for his own, so the produce takes on the gentile's status. By the same logic, the gentile may have swapped the Jew's wine for his own wine. Then the deposited wine should be fully forbidden like סתם יינם, even for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when the land rests

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
One who deposits his produce with a gentile,
they are like the produce of the gentile
regarding the seventh year and regarding tithes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the permission to benefit given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that wine deposited with a gentile is permitted for benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If deposited produce is treated as the gentile's own because of a possible swap, deposited wine should be treated as gentile wine and forbidden even for benefit.

steps.title: The gentile set aside a special corner for the wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the gentile set aside a קרן זוית for the Jew's wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the gentile set aside a corner for the Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the ברייתא to a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine was kept in a separate corner set aside for the Jew, the worry that the gentile swapped it mostly goes away. So it is not treated like the gentile's own wine, and benefit is permitted. The משנה about produce is talking about an ordinary deposit with no special place.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, as in a case where

phrases.english: For example, where he set aside a corner for him.
phrases.notes: The gentile set aside a special corner just for the Jew's wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about any deposit, so the worry of swapping should forbid the wine completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a deposit kept in a corner set aside for the Jew, so there is no real worry of swapping.

steps.title: If so, drinking should be permitted too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the wine was kept in a special corner, why is drinking still forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, drinking should also be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the answer from the other side. If the worry is gone, the wine should be fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 removed the reason to forbid benefit. But the same logic seems to remove the reason to forbid drinking too. So why does the ברייתא still forbid drinking? The next step brings support for this question.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case

phrases.english: If so,
drinking should also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 by taking it to its logical end.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ban on drinking, once it is set in a case with a special corner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A designated corner removes the worry of swapping, so there is no reason left to forbid drinking.

steps.title: בר קפרא's teaching permits drinking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its question with a story: רבי יוחנן came to פרוד and asked for בר קפרא's teachings, and רבי תנחום taught that deposited wine is מותר בשתיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן came to פרוד and said: Is there any teaching of בר קפרא here? רבי תנחום of פרוד taught him: One who deposits his wine with a gentile, it is permitted to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of בר קפרא that permits drinking deposited wine. This backs up the question of step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is real support that such wine can be permitted even for drinking. Presumably בר קפרא is talking about a case like the special corner. So the question gets stronger: why does our ברייתא forbid drinking?
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מִשְׁנָה does not mean our משנה of רבי. It means the collection of teachings that בר קפרא taught.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan happened to come to Parod,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ מִשְׁנַת בַּר קַפָּרָא?
phrases.english: He said: Is there any teaching of Bar Kappara (here)?

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא לֵיהּ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם דְּמִן פָּרוֹד:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum from Parod taught him:
One who deposits his wine with a gentile:
it is permitted to drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the question of step 5 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That wine deposited with a gentile (in a safe setup) can be permitted even for drinking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בר קפרא, as taught by רבי תנחום of פרוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are two ברייתות that disagree about drinking. רבי זירא resolves this in step 8.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praises the student with the פסוק of the fallen tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן applied to רבי תנחום the פסוק "where the tree falls, there it shall be," explaining that it means the tree's fruits remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read about him: "The place where the tree falls, there it shall be." Could you think it means the tree itself will be there? Rather, its fruits will be there.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short side story. רבי יוחנן praises רבי תנחום for carrying on the teachings of his late teacher, בר קפרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is obvious that a fallen tree lies where it fell, so the פסוק must mean something more. The "tree" is the great חכם who has passed away, and the "fruits" are his students who keep his Torah alive in his place. This does not change the הלכה. It honors the source that was just quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? Meaning: surely not

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the sources clash: our ברייתא forbids drinking deposited wine, while בר קפרא permits it. The next step, by רבי זירא, resolves this. The story ends by honoring רבי תנחום as the "fruit" who carries on בר קפרא's Torah.

phrases.english: He read about him (the verse):
"The place where the tree falls, there it shall be."
"There it shall be": could that enter your mind?
phrases.notes: Of course a fallen tree stays where it fell, so the פסוק can't just mean that.

phrases.english: Rather, there its fruits shall be.
phrases.notes: The fruits are the students, like רבי תנחום, who carry on the teacher's Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ מְקוֹם שֶׁיִּפּוֹל הָעֵץ שָׁם יְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 6 with רבי יוחנן's reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם's students are his "fruits," who keep his Torah alive after he is gone.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers the contradiction. The source that permits drinking the deposited wine follows רבי אליעזר, and the source that forbids it follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is not difficult. This source follows רבי אליעזר, and that source follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the clash between the ברייתא רבי תנחום taught, which permits drinking, and the earlier ruling that forbids drinking. He says each source matches a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither source is wrong. They just reflect two sides of a real מחלוקת. The proof that this מחלוקת exists comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer
This one ... that one; matches each source to its own opinion
The Rabbis; the majority opinion against a single תנא

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult —
this follows Rabbi Eliezer, that follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The permitting ברייתא is רבי אליעזר's view. The forbidding ruling is רבנן's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by the story of רבי תנחום
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to reflect one view, so they contradicted each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source follows a different side of a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבנן

steps.title: The ברייתא about a house in a gentile's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת. A Jew bought or rented a house in a gentile's courtyard and filled it with wine, with the key or seal in his hand. רבי אליעזר permits the wine and חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Whether someone buys or rents a house in a gentile's courtyard and fills it with wine, with the key or the seal in the Jew's hand, רבי אליעזר permits it and חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי אליעזר and רבנן really disagree about wine kept in a gentile's area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wine is locked or sealed and the Jew controls access, which is even safer than a special corner. Still, חכמים forbid it, because the gentile lives right there. רבי אליעזר trusts the lock or seal.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse רבי אליעזר here with רבי אלעזר in step 11. They are two different people.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Both one who buys and one who rents
a house in a gentile's courtyard,
and they filled it with wine,
and the key or seal is in the Jew's hand —
Rabbi Eliezer permits, and the Sages forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי זירא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבנן disagree about wine guarded in a gentile's area
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a house in a gentile's courtyard with key or seal held by the Jew

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of names, with several versions of who said it, the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. A Jew's locked or sealed wine in a gentile's courtyard is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא son of רבי חייא בר נחמני said that רב חסדא said in the name of רב. Some say רב חסדא said it in the name of זעירי. Some say רב חסדא said: אבא בר חמא told me that זעירי said this: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי אליעזר. The long list of names just records the different versions of who said this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three versions agree on the ruling itself. They only differ on whether it came from רב or from זעירי, and through whom. So in practice the sealed or locked wine is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Practical bottom line: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, so wine guarded by a key or seal in a gentile's courtyard is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya, son of Rabbi Chiya bar Nachmani, said,
Rav Chisda said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר זְעֵירִי,
phrases.english: and some say Rav Chisda said that Ze'eiri said,
and some say Rav Chisda said:
Abba bar Chama told me,
this is what Ze'eiri said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת quoted in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה כרבי אליעזר: wine guarded by key or seal in a gentile's courtyard is permitted

steps.title: Is one seal enough to protect wine?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says everything is protected by one seal except wine. רבי יוחנן says even wine is protected by one seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Everything is guarded by one seal, except wine, which is not guarded by one seal. And רבי יוחנן said: Even wine is guarded by one seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between two אמוראים about whether a single seal is enough security for wine left with a gentile. This sets up the next step, which links them to the earlier מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר treats wine as special. A gentile is more tempted to tamper with wine, so one seal isn't enough. רבי יוחנן says one seal works for wine just like everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: One seal (as opposed to a double seal)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַכֹּל מִשְׁתַּמֵּר בְּחוֹתָם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Everything is guarded by one seal,
except for wine,
which is not guarded by one seal.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even wine is guarded by one seal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַכֹּל מִשְׁתַּמֵּר בְּחוֹתָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related אמורא-level disagreement about sealing wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: one seal is not enough for wine. רבי יוחנן: one seal is enough even for wine.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן follow the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן don't truly argue on their own. רבי יוחנן follows רבי אליעזר, and רבי אלעזר follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: this one follows רבי אליעזר, and that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the disagreement in step 11 is really the same מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבנן from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן, who says one seal is enough, matches רבי אליעזר, who permits sealed wine. רבי אלעזר, who says one seal is not enough, matches רבנן, who forbid it. Each אמורא is simply reporting a different תנא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree (on their own; each follows an earlier view)

steps.whatToRemember: The same מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבנן explains both the clash of the sources (step 8) and the clash between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree —
this one follows Rabbi Eliezer, that one follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן (one seal works) is like רבי אליעזר. רבי אלעזר (one seal isn't enough) is like רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two אמוראים of step 11 by tying them to the ברייתא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching each אמורא to an earlier תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן seemed to have their own independent argument
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי אליעזר; רבי אלעזר follows רבנן

steps.title: A second version: the argument is about a double seal
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argued about a double seal (חוֹתָם בְּתוֹךְ חוֹתָם), not a single seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבי אלעזר says a double seal protects everything except wine, and wine is not protected even by a double seal. רבי יוחנן says even wine is protected by a double seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the argument from step 11. In this version the two אמוראים argue about a double seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the argument was about one seal. Here the bar is higher, a seal within a seal. רבי אלעזר still treats wine more strictly than everything else, and רבי יוחנן says a double seal is enough even for wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A seal within a seal: double protection

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In step 11 the argument was about one seal; in this version it is about a double seal.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabbi Elazar says:
Everything is protected by a seal within a seal,
except wine,
which is not protected by a seal within a seal.
And Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן מִשְׁתַּמֵּר בְּחוֹתָם בְּתוֹךְ חוֹתָם.
phrases.english: Even wine is protected by a seal within a seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the argument from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: wine is not protected even by a double seal. רבי יוחנן: wine is protected by a double seal.

steps.title: Both opinions follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: In this version, both רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר follow רבנן; they argue about how far רבנן went.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both follow רבנן. One (רבי יוחנן) holds that רבנן argued with רבי אליעזר only about one seal, but they permit a double seal. The other (רבי אלעזר) holds that רבנן forbid even a double seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how this second version fits with the ברייתא. Here both אמוראים follow רבנן, but they read רבנן differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, רבי יוחנן followed רבי אליעזר. Now both agree with רבנן that one seal is not enough. Their only question is whether רבנן also forbid a double seal.

phrases.english: And both of them follow the Rabbis.
One Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This first "one Sage" is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: When the Rabbis argue with Rabbi Eliezer,
it is about one seal,
but with a seal within a seal they permit it.
And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This second one is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: They forbid even a seal within a seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which side of the ברייתא each אמורא follows in the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both opinions are placed inside one side of the ברייתא (רבנן), with different readings of how far רבנן went.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on step 12, one might think רבי יוחנן must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this version both follow רבנן; they only argue about whether רבנן forbid a double seal.

steps.title: What counts as a seal within a seal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical picture of a double seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a seal within a seal look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a double seal looks like in real life. This sets up רבא's examples in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13 and 14 used the term חותם בתוך חותם without defining it. Before the rule can be used, we need to know which kinds of packing count.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What does a seal within a seal look like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the term used in the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical definition of a double seal.

steps.title: רבא's examples of a double seal
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives three cases: a basin over a barrel, a basket over a barrel, and a wineskin in a sack.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: A basin over the barrel's mouth that is smeared with clay and sealed is a double seal; if not, it is not. A basket that is tied tight is a double seal; if it is not tied tight, it is not. A wineskin in a sack: if its sealed mouth faces down, it is a double seal; if it faces up, it is not. And if he bends its neck inward, ties it and seals it, it is a double seal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with three everyday ways of packing wine. For each one he says when it counts as a double seal and when it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that there must be two separate barriers that are each hard to open without it being noticed. A loose cover or a mouth facing up is easy to reach, so it does not add a real second seal.
steps.whatToRemember: A double seal means two real barriers. A cover counts only if it is tightly closed or sealed, and a wineskin counts only if its mouth is hidden (facing down or bent inward and sealed).

phrases.english: Rava says:
A basin over the mouth of a barrel
that is smeared with clay and sealed
is a seal within a seal,
and if not, it is not.
A basket that is fastened tight
is a seal within a seal;
if it is not fastened tight,
it is not a seal within a seal.
A wineskin in a sack:
if its sealed mouth faces down,
it is a seal within a seal;
if its mouth faces up,
it is not a seal within a seal.
And if he bends its neck inward
and ties it and seals it,
phrases.notes: He means he ties up and seals the sack around the wineskin.

phrases.english: it is a seal within a seal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three practical cases: a sealed basin, a tightly fastened basket, and a wineskin with its mouth down or bent in and sealed.

steps.title: The חכמים changed their ruling on wine from certain towns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: at first wine from three towns was forbidden because of nearby non-Jewish villages; later only open barrels were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: At first they used to say wine from עין כושי is forbidden because of בירת סריקא, wine from ברקתא because of כפר פרשאי, and wine from זגדור because of כפר שלים. Later they changed and said: open barrels are forbidden, sealed barrels are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens a new topic. It tells how the חכמים first forbade wine from three towns and later changed their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each town was next to a non-Jewish village, so there was worry that non-Jews had touched the wine. The later ruling split the case: open barrels stay forbidden, but sealed barrels are allowed. The reason for the change comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back and said (they changed their ruling)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
At first they used to say:
Wine from Ein Kushi is forbidden
because of Birat Serika,
and wine from Barkata is forbidden
because of the village of Parshai,
and wine from Zagdor is forbidden
because of the village of Shaleim.
They changed and said:
Open barrels are forbidden;
sealed ones are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic about sealed wine near non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Final ruling: open barrels from these towns are forbidden, sealed barrels are permitted.

steps.title: Why did the ruling change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים thought at first and what they thought in the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they think at first, and what did they think in the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind both rulings in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us the rulings but not the reasons. The גמרא wants to know what new understanding made the חכמים permit sealed barrels.

phrases.english: At first, what did they think,
and in the end, what did they think?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי סְבוּר, וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי סְבוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the original ruling and the later change.

steps.title: כותים do guard their sealed barrels
steps.stepSummary: At first they thought כותים don't care about a non-Jew's touch at all; later they realized כותים do care about sealed barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they thought: a כותי doesn't care if a non-Jew touches his wine, whether the barrels are open or sealed. In the end they thought: he doesn't care about open barrels, but about sealed barrels he does care.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both rulings. The change came from a new understanding of how careful the כותים are with sealed wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the worry covered all the wine, because they thought the כותים would let non-Jews touch anything. Later they saw that the כותים guard sealed barrels, so those can be trusted. Open barrels stay forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling depends on how the כותים act: they guard sealed barrels from non-Jews, so sealed barrels are permitted, but open ones are forbidden.

phrases.english: At first they thought:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוּתִי מַקְפִּיד עַל מַגַּע גּוֹי,
phrases.english: A Samaritan doesn't care about a non-Jew's touch,
no difference whether open barrels
or sealed barrels.
And in the end they thought:
When he doesn't care, that is only about open barrels,
but about sealed barrels he certainly does care.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סְבוּר: אֵין כּוּתִי מַקְפִּיד עַל מַגַּע גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The change came from realizing that כותים are careful to keep non-Jews away from their sealed barrels, though not from open ones.

steps.title: Are sealed barrels really permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ruling that sealed barrels are permitted and introduces a contradicting source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are sealed barrels really permitted? Here is a contradiction:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It doubts that sealed barrels are permitted and tells us a contradicting source is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's final ruling forbade only open barrels, so sealed barrels were allowed. Step 19 explained why: the כותים are careful about sealed barrels. The גמרא now signals that another source seems to forbid even sealed barrels. The actual source comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: "And I will throw against it." A formula that introduces a source which contradicts what was just said.

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is not a real request for information. It is the start of a challenge, and the contradicting source has not been quoted yet. It comes next.

phrases.english: And are sealed barrels permitted?
phrases.notes: This points back to the end of the ברייתא, which forbade only open barrels, so sealed ones were allowed.

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final ruling of the ברייתא (and the reasoning in step 19) that sealed barrels are permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's final ruling that only open barrels are forbidden, so sealed barrels are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source, about to be quoted, appears to forbid sealed barrels. That would contradict the ruling that they are permitted.
